title: The Alhambra Ballroom on 126th Street
summary: The Alhambra was an upstairs former taxi dance hall with a slow elevator; Russell played its multi-band night of September 13, 1929.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Now, what can you tell me about the Alhambra Ballroom? Didn't you play there with Russell?
Yeah, I worked there. It was a ballroom, just like it said. It used to be a taxi dance hall.
It used to be a taxi dance hall, and then they changed it into a ballroom. Jelly Roll Morton's band worked there a while. Not long.
Here in one of the liner notes it says that "Luis Russell's orchestra was one of those featured at the Alhambra Ballroom in Harlem on the night of Friday the Thirteenth of September, 1929."
Mmm, could be. Sure. Well, that's one of them nights when they had three or four or five or six different bands, you know. We happened to be one of them.
Do you remember where it was?
Yeah. 126th Street and 7th Avenue. Right on the corner, upstairs.

Yeah. Nothin' to see, really. You had to take an elevator to get up there. Lord help it, if a fire had ever happened or anything. They had to ...(?)... the people, and they had to wait for the elevator to come out of there. It would take you longer to get out the place than you'd stand in there at night! It was terrible. They didn't have big fires in them days, I guess. Luckily, nothing ever happened. It was a beautiful-looking place, too. Nice ballroom. Beautiful.
Of course, with the opening they would make it more festive by having several bands. But was there usually one band or two bands at the Alhambra?

Well, let me see. As a rule, I think they used two when they started off. I mean, as a general rule every night I think they had two bands. Maybe when the business fell off, they used one band. But I'm sure that they used two bands. After the opening night. You know, they had all the big things opening night. Then they went into the regular routine with two bands. And then as business fell off and got worse, then they used one band.
Now, the Savoy was already going.
So they were copying the Savoy in a sense.

I don't know if the Savoy wasn't running that place, strictly speaking. They could have been backers. I'm not sure. I'm not sure that they weren't. I never got mixed up in the business of the places. As long as the place was open and hired me, that's all I was interested in.
